mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 8% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% for three consecutive months signals a strengthening manufacturing sector, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when INDPRO exceeds its 12-month MA by >1.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 jobs combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate by at least 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month by >100000 AND UNRATE > previous month by >0.3pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction-related equities and drags on broader market returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month MA by >10% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during such housing downturn episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recessionary period (UNRATE > 7%) signals a policy-driven monetary easing, which lowers long-term interest rates and supports equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during such easing episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% while consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is below 1% for three consecutive months signals a supply-side expansion without inflationary pressure, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month by >0.5% AND CPIAUCSL < previous month by any amount AND CPIAUCSL < 100 for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) under these conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in the unemployment rate above 8% that persists for two consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which reduces consumer demand and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during such periods.
